BLD-lock_after_guard.content:
The lock SHALL be taken at process start, immediately after the workspace root is resolved and its sentinel,
`photos-00-workspace-guard`, is verified.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-lock_after_guard.title: The lock follows the workspace guard

BLD-lock_owner_record.content:
The lock SHALL record the identity of the process that owns it and the time it started, so that a lock whose owner is
gone can be told from one whose owner is running.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-lock_owner_record.title: The lock records its owner

BLD-one_snapshot_mechanism.content:
The three phases SHALL take their snapshots through one mechanism — prep §14.3, geotag §29 and merge §10.3 invoke it,
and none redefines it.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-one_snapshot_mechanism.title: One snapshot mechanism for every phase

BLD-phase_commands.content:
The phases SHALL be the commands `photos-cartographer prep`, `geotag` and `merge` — named in the specs, and in their
records, `photos-1-prep`, `photos-2-geotag` and `photos-3-merge`.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phase_commands.title: The phases are three commands

BLD-phases_inside_lock.content:
Each phase's `plan`, `dry-run` and `execute` SHALL run with the lock taken at start already held; none SHALL take it
again or scope it on its own (prep §14, geotag §29).
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-phases_inside_lock.title: The phases run inside the run's lock

BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.content:
The snapshot SHALL be a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block of the workspace configuration,
`photos-00-config.json`; with no `zfs` block, or one not enabled, none is taken. Its name SHALL carry the plan id.
`snapshots_required` decides what a failed snapshot means: true, the run aborts before its first change; false, or the
block not configured, it proceeds without one.
sections: Shared — how this build does it
BLD-snapshot_is_zfs.title: The snapshot is a ZFS snapshot, configured by the `zfs` block

CHC-ask_only_what_data_cannot_settle.content: Resolve everything derivable automatically; ask only real judgment questions, and make each one cheap to answer.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-ask_only_what_data_cannot_settle.title: Ask only what the data can't settle

CHC-local_folder_library.content:
The destination is a plain directory tree on disk (feeds digiKam or Immich), not a cloud service or proprietary
catalog.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-local_folder_library.title: A local, owned, folder-based library

CHC-photos_matter.content: Because they matter, no original may be lost or silently altered — correctness beats convenience.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-photos_matter.title: Photos matter; they are irreplaceable, so they deserve care

CHC-total_placement.content:
Every photo ends up on the map — precise where tracks allow, rough or manual where they don't — so the result is a
*map-complete* library, not just the frames that came with a location.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
CHC-total_placement.title: 100% placement, even under GPS scarcity

DEF-geotag.content:
**Geotag**, the second phase, resolves each photo to its true time, inferring and correcting each camera's clock
offset; places the photos that carry no position along the recorded tracks; and renames each by its corrected local
time.
DEF-geotag.title: Geotag

DEF-library.content:
The **library** is the permanent, curated collection the media ends in — outside every workspace, and written only by
merge.
DEF-library.title: The library

DEF-merge.content:
**Merge**, the third phase, runs after a workspace has been geotagged and finalized: it moves the finalized media,
sorted by destination, into the library — never renaming or overwriting anything already there — and then seals the
workspace.
DEF-merge.title: Merge

DEF-prep.content:
**Prep**, the first phase, takes an unorganized dump and makes it a clean working set: it consolidates the dump,
normalizes extensions, sets duplicates aside (recoverably, never deleting), organizes the media by date, and hands
geotag what it found.
DEF-prep.title: Prep

DEF-workspace.content:
A **workspace** is the transient place one ingest happens in: a dump of media enters it, the phases work on it in
turn, and merge empties it into the library. Every run acts on exactly one workspace.
DEF-workspace.title: The workspace

FCT-clocks_drift.content:
Each body's clock is wrong by its own amount, and that amount changes between days (drift, manual resets to local time
in the morning, missed DST). There is no single global offset to find.

*Where one has met it:* The import that landed an hour early; the shots an hour off after a border; a day's frames
scattered because the clock was never set — blamed on negligence or forgetfulness, not on a category.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
FCT-clocks_drift.title: Camera clocks drift — independently, and from day to day

FCT-large_batches.content:
A trip dump or a years-deep library is big and mixed: many RAW/JPEG frames across multiple cameras and phones.

*Where one has met it:* The card one keeps meaning to deal with; the decade of folders; or *"I'll geotag these
someday."*
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
FCT-large_batches.title: A photo batch is large — thousands of frames, several cameras

FCT-partial_track_coverage.content:
The logger's tracks reach *some* of the library, never all of it — so the track alone can never place every frame; the
rest needs fallbacks.

*Where one has met it:* The half-tagged library; the map view with holes where phone-sync missed; the frames that came
with a pin and the many that didn't.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
FCT-partial_track_coverage.title: GPX coverage is partial

INV-one_run_at_a_time.content:
At most one cartographer run SHALL act on a workspace at any time — whatever the commands: two runs of one phase, runs
of two phases, a merge, a finalize, or a quarantine prune.
INV-one_run_at_a_time.title: One run at a time

RAT-camera_groups_generated.content: **Camera groups are generated for the user**, ready to paste — leaving only the judgment, not the derivation.
RAT-camera_groups_generated.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-camera_groups_generated.title: The tedious part of a judgment call should be pre-computed

RAT-clustering_details.content:
**The consensus-clustering details** of clock-offset inference — clustering rather than averaging is forced by
robustness, but the spread thresholds, the tie-breaks, and the confidence grades are choices.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-clustering_details.title: The consensus-clustering details

RAT-configurable_folder_names.content:
**Defaults that are offered, not imposed.** Folder names (`0-sources … 6-photos-by-dest`) are configurable, not
hardcoded — the seven-stage *structure* is the invariant, the *labels* are the operator's. The rigidity is structural
where it must be and accommodating where it can afford to be.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-configurable_folder_names.title: Defaults that are offered, not imposed

RAT-consolidated_log.content:
A **consolidated, self-describing log in one kept folder** — *traceability arrived at, not chosen* (and it is this
traceability that lets the provenance tag above mean anything).
RAT-consolidated_log.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-consolidated_log.title: A choice made weeks earlier must still explain itself on return

RAT-coordinate_carries_its_method.content:
Completeness means precision now *varies* across the library — so each placement must declare how trustworthy it is
(via the **traceability** the multi-session reality forces — see below).

**Every coordinate carries its derivation method** — native / GPX direct-match / interpolated / extrapolated / manual
— so a rough pin is never mistaken for a precise one.

*Why it is kept:* "I still want to be able to know, at a later date, how that GPS position was assigned - maybe I want
to refine it by image/place recognition for example." A new track needs no tag: it changes the GPX folder, which makes
the GPS decisions stale, and they are regenerated.

*The traceability:* "every decision must be traced, and by incorporating the precision, I allow it even in the final
library."
RAT-coordinate_carries_its_method.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-coordinate_carries_its_method.title: Completeness means precision now *varies* across the library

RAT-decision_withdrawable.content:
A **pre-state ledger** records what a file held before a manual override, so deleting the decision *restores* the
prior state.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decision_withdrawable.title: A decision must be withdrawable

RAT-decisions_cascade.content:
Decisions **cascade**: *one far-reaching choice high in the tree is traded for many short-reaching ones* — inherit
unless overridden, remembered across re-runs. (This is where "far-reaching" comes from — a chosen trade, not an
inherent property.)
RAT-decisions_cascade.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decisions_cascade.title: Asking per-photo would be thousands of short-reaching chores

RAT-decisions_reread_cache_only.content:
Decisions are **idempotently re-read each run**; the fast store is **SQLite as a cache only** — derived, rebuildable,
never the source of truth.
RAT-decisions_reread_cache_only.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decisions_reread_cache_only.title: Resuming must not mean re-deciding

RAT-decoded_pixel_identity.content: A **decoded-pixel fingerprint** (ImageMagick/ffmpeg), not file bytes, as each photo's stable identity.
RAT-decoded_pixel_identity.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-decoded_pixel_identity.title: Identity must survive EXIF rewrites and renames

RAT-destination_tree_is_a_hierarchy.content:
The destination tree must be a **hierarchy** — the cascade rides on folder nesting, so a flat or tag-based layout can't
inherit at all, and every value would fall back to per-photo entry.
RAT-destination_tree_is_a_hierarchy.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-destination_tree_is_a_hierarchy.title: Inheritance needs an axis to travel along

RAT-discrete_stages.content:
**Discrete, inspectable stages** (the numbered pipeline) — each a real checkpoint; the **filesystem is treated as
truth**.
RAT-discrete_stages.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-discrete_stages.title: A crash must be recoverable

RAT-durable_record.content:
That, in turn, forces the record machinery — and note what is *not* a driver here: auditability and decade-longevity,
are **zero-cost benefits** that fall out of building for resumability.
RAT-durable_record.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-durable_record.title: Durable, resumable record

RAT-editor_writes_only_decisions.content: The editor writes **only the `user_decision` field** — never derived or evidence fields.
RAT-editor_writes_only_decisions.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-editor_writes_only_decisions.title: The record must stay an honest statement of *intent*, not a mutable scratchpad

RAT-folder_gps_fallback.content:
A **cascading folder-level GPS fallback** — set one coordinate at a trip's root and it is inherited down the tree (P3
makes this cheap; one answer covers many photos).
RAT-folder_gps_fallback.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-folder_gps_fallback.title: Placement cannot depend on the track alone

RAT-format_editor_split.content: **Format + editor split**: JSON is the record; the Time/Drift/GPS app is what writes it.
RAT-format_editor_split.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-format_editor_split.title: Intricate, evidence-specific decisions are too error-prone to hand-edit

RAT-idempotent_reruns.content: **Idempotent, diff-based** re-runs; a run over unchanged state is a no-op.
RAT-idempotent_reruns.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-idempotent_reruns.title: Re-runs must not redo settled work or cause churn

RAT-linux_and_open_source_not_roots.content:
This is built and run on Linux, but Linux is not a root — the design is plain Python shelling out to `exiftool`,
ImageMagick, and `ffmpeg`, all cross-platform, so it would port with little structural change. Open-source is likewise
a downstream expression of the "local, owned" ethos (P1, P2), not a structural driver. Neither forces anything below.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-linux_and_open_source_not_roots.title: Linux and open-source are not roots

RAT-lock_and_revalidation.content:
This whole-run lock is independent of, and stricter than, the dependency-revalidation discipline: revalidation guards
against *stale* inputs across separate runs, while the lock guarantees runs never overlap in the first place.
RAT-lock_and_revalidation.title: The lock and revalidation guard different things

RAT-longevity_is_free.content: *(zero-cost benefit)* Decade-longevity and "open one folder years later" come free — incidental, never the driver.
RAT-longevity_is_free.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-longevity_is_free.title: Built to survive a three-week gap, it survives a thirty-year one

RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.content:
Such intricacy would be brutal to enter by hand, so P3 (ask only what the data can't settle) governs how it is
collected — and introduces the document's central trade.
RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-minimal_cascading_asks.title: Minimal, cascading asks

RAT-multi_session_job.content:
This is a **two-level chain**: a fact and a choice together force an intermediate consequence, and that consequence
forces the record machinery. It is the part most easily mistaken for an arbitrary choice.

Neither root does it alone. Scale (F1) without the 100%-coverage goal (P4) is fast: prep is automated, one keeps the
native-GPS frames, lets the track cover the easy matches, and stops — plausibly one sitting, because the long tail is
never chased. The goal without scale is also trivial: placing ten photos completely takes minutes. Only *total
coverage across a large, mixed batch* produces a long tail of per-(camera, destination, day) offset confirmations and
hand-placed remainder that cannot be finished in one sitting.

Note: not all of that elapsed time is P4's. The album **sort** into a destination tree is owed to **P2** — one would
drag photos into folders even with no geotagging at all — so P2 contributes session-spanning human time on its own.
What F1 + P4 *specifically* add is the **long tail of confirmations and manual placement** that has no automated
escape. Either way, the job likely spans multiple sessions.

**Intermediate consequence — a multi-session job.** The machine cannot hold one's decisions in its head between
sittings.
RAT-multi_session_job.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-multi_session_job.title: A multi-session job

RAT-no_automatic_deletion.content: Duplicates are **quarantined**, never removed; pruning is an explicit, separate act.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-no_automatic_deletion.title: Deletion is never automatic

RAT-no_mutation_outside_plan.content: **plan → validate → execute**; the dry-run *is* the serialized plan; stale plans are rejected against current state.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-no_mutation_outside_plan.title: No mutation outside a validated plan

RAT-non_destructive_core.content: plan / validate / execute; atomic no-clobber; quarantine, not delete; pre-state ledger.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-non_destructive_core.title: Non-destructive core

RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.content:
Start with the fact. Because each camera's clock is wrong by its own amount, and that amount changes from day to day
(F2), there is no single offset to discover — the correct answer is **per (camera group, destination, day)**. *That*
granularity is the entire source of the decisions' "complexity": it is a consequence of real, time-varying drift, not a
premise.

The offset is **inferred and applied per (camera group, destination, day)**; corrections fall *between* destinations,
never within one — which is why **one destination = one coherent shoot**.
RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-offset_per_camera_destination_day.title: Drift is per-camera and per-day, so no global offset is correct

RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.content:
The mechanism is named for ZFS because that is the reference implementation, but it is deliberately the *only* part
of the pipeline that touches a specific filesystem feature, and it is optional; everything else is filesystem-agnostic.
RAT-one_filesystem_specific_part.title: Why the snapshot alone may touch the filesystem

RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.content: Each phase that mutates uses the same mechanism so the phases behave identically and cannot diverge.
RAT-one_snapshot_mechanism.title: One mechanism, so the phases cannot diverge

RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.content:
Timezone, clock offset, and GPS fallback are **piggybacked on the destination sort** one would do anyway for real albums
(P2).
RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.section_name: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
sections: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-piggyback_on_the_destination_sort.title: The unavoidable human act should pay for itself

RAT-plain_json_record.content: **Plain JSON** decision artifacts — the durable external record, read back at the start of each session.
RAT-plain_json_record.section_name: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
sections: From F1 + P4 — total coverage at scale becomes a multi-session job
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-plain_json_record.title: Decisions can't live in the tool between sessions, so they must persist outside it

RAT-planning_inside_lock.content:
Planning is non-mutating, but it must still not run concurrently: a plan computed against a workspace another process
is reading or mutating is untrustworthy, so planning is inside the lock too.
RAT-planning_inside_lock.title: A plan made beside another run cannot be trusted

RAT-recoverable_core.content:
Crash-recovery follows from P1 (an interrupted run must never strand an original half-changed); the diff-based
idempotency also answers F3 — because coverage is partial, one adds more tracks or photos later and re-runs, so a run
must act only on what actually changed.
RAT-recoverable_core.section_name: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
sections: From P1 + F3 — recoverable, and resumable on incremental input
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-recoverable_core.title: Recoverable core

RAT-remainder_worklist.content:
An explicit, short **remainder worklist** — what no evidence can locate is collected for a manual pin, not left off the
map.
RAT-remainder_worklist.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-remainder_worklist.title: The true unplaceable set must be surfaced, never silently dropped

RAT-safety_not_on_the_plan.content: No-clobber **re-verified atomically at the moment of each write**, not just at plan time.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-safety_not_on_the_plan.title: Safety cannot rest on the plan being correct

RAT-snapshot_is_extra.content:
**Snapshots are an optional extra safety layer, not a requirement.** The pipeline operates fully and safely without
them: correctness and recoverability rest on the journal, recoverable quarantine, no-clobber operations, and
filesystem-as-truth reconciliation. Snapshots add a clean-slate rollback path on top of those for operators whose
filesystem supports it; they are not the basis of the safety model.
RAT-snapshot_is_extra.title: A snapshot is an extra layer, not the safety model

RAT-stage_cut_points.content:
**The exact decomposition into seven stages** rather than six or eight. The *principle* of discrete inspectable
checkpoints is forced (P1+F3); the specific cut points are judgment.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-stage_cut_points.title: The exact decomposition into stages

RAT-total_coverage_cascade.content:
This choice fights F3: tracks cover only *part* of the library, but the output must be *whole*. That gap is what forces
the fallback machinery to exist: without P4, tracks alone would be the entire story and everything below would be
unnecessary.
RAT-total_coverage_cascade.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-total_coverage_cascade.title: Total-coverage cascade

RAT-track_squeezed.content:
**Direct match → interpolation between points → bounded extrapolation off the ends**, each used before falling back to
manual.
RAT-track_squeezed.section_name: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
sections: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-track_squeezed.title: Every placeable point of the track must be squeezed out

RAT-which_folder_library.content:
**The downstream library, not the tree.** A *hierarchical* destination tree is **forced**, not chosen: the timezone /
offset / GPS-fallback cascade rides on the folder nesting, so a flat or tag-based layout would make inheritance
impossible and drive the per-photo workload straight back up. What is actually free is only *which* folder-based
library consumes the result — digiKam, or any other — and the cosmetic naming of the levels.
sections: Philosophy — the roots, and what they force
RAT-which_folder_library.title: The downstream library, not the tree

RUL-every_command_locks.content:
A workspace SHALL have exactly one lock, shared by every command. Every command that reads or changes the workspace
SHALL hold it while it does.
RUL-every_command_locks.title: One lock, taken by every command

RUL-filesystem_agnostic.content:
Nothing in cartographer but the snapshot SHALL depend on a particular filesystem's features; and cartographer SHALL run
fully on a filesystem that has none.
RUL-filesystem_agnostic.omit_reason: a design constraint over the whole code; the gap audit (backlog item 2) checks it
RUL-filesystem_agnostic.title: Only the snapshot depends on the filesystem

RUL-lock_before_reading.content:
A run SHALL hold the lock before it reads any of the workspace's content — before it plans, scans, fingerprints,
reads metadata, dry-runs or executes. Planning changes nothing, and is inside the lock all the same.
RUL-lock_before_reading.title: The lock comes before anything is read

RUL-lock_fail_fast.content:
A run that finds the workspace locked SHALL NOT wait for it. It SHALL stop at once, saying the workspace is locked by a
run in progress, having scanned, planned and changed nothing — and having produced no plan, no dry-run report and no
artifact.
RUL-lock_fail_fast.title: A locked workspace is refused at once

RUL-lock_released_on_any_end.content: A run SHALL release the lock when it ends, whether it succeeds or fails.
RUL-lock_released_on_any_end.title: The lock is released however the run ends

RUL-lock_through_the_run.content:
A run SHALL hold the lock until it ends — through planning, dry run, execution, and every record and artifact it
writes — and SHALL release it then. The lock SHALL NOT outlive its run: between runs, the workspace is unlocked.
RUL-lock_through_the_run.title: The lock lasts the whole run, and no longer

RUL-merge_snapshots_library.content: Prep's and geotag's snapshot SHALL cover the workspace; merge's SHALL cover the library, where its changes land.
RUL-merge_snapshots_library.omit_reason: carried by merge's own snapshot items, when merge is converted
RUL-merge_snapshots_library.title: Merge snapshots the library

RUL-required_snapshot_or_nothing.content: When the configuration requires snapshots, a run that cannot take one SHALL stop before it changes anything.
RUL-required_snapshot_or_nothing.title: A required snapshot that fails stops the run

RUL-snapshot_off_by_default.content: Snapshots SHALL be off unless the workspace's configuration turns them on.
RUL-snapshot_off_by_default.title: No snapshot unless configured

RUL-snapshot_optional.content:
A phase that changes files MAY first take a snapshot of what it is about to change, from which the whole change can be
rolled back. Cartographer SHALL be complete and safe without one: no guarantee SHALL depend on a snapshot having been
taken.
RUL-snapshot_optional.title: A snapshot is optional, and nothing rests on it

RUL-snapshot_per_plan.content: Each snapshot SHALL be identifiable by the plan whose changes it precedes.
RUL-snapshot_per_plan.title: A snapshot names its plan

RUL-snapshot_timing.content:
A snapshot SHALL be taken after the plan has been validated against its dependencies and the lock is held, and before
the plan's first change.
RUL-snapshot_timing.title: When a snapshot is taken

RUL-stale_lock_recovered.content:
A lock left behind by a run that died SHALL be recognisable as stale, and recoverable, so that a crash never leaves a
workspace locked for good.
RUL-stale_lock_recovered.title: A stale lock is recognised and recovered

RUL-stale_takeover_conservative.content:
A stale lock SHALL be taken over only when its owner is provably gone. A lock whose owner may still be running SHALL be
left alone.
RUL-stale_takeover_conservative.title: Only a dead owner's lock is taken over

RUL-unrequired_snapshot_proceeds.content:
When snapshots are not required, or not configured, a run SHALL proceed without one. Its safety then rests, as it
always does, on the journal, the recoverable quarantine, never overwriting, and the filesystem as the truth.
RUL-unrequired_snapshot_proceeds.title: Without a required snapshot, the run goes on

arch.description: Mapping of uml key to uml content.

constraints.description: List of constraint names, which are defined for this need.

constraints_error.description: An error message set if any constraint failed, and `error_message` field is set in config.

constraints_passed.description: True if all constraints passed, False if any failed, None if not yet checked.

constraints_results.description: Mapping of constraint name, to check name, to result, None if not yet checked.

content.description: The main content of the need.

docname.description: Name of the document where the need is defined (None if external).

doctype.description: The markup type of the content, denoted by the suffix of the source file, e.g. '.rst'.

external_css.description: CSS class name, added to the external reference.

external_url.description: URL of the need, if it is an external need.

has_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list.

has_forbidden_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list, and the link type does not allow dead links.

is_external.description: If true, no node is created and need is referencing external url.

is_import.description: If true, the need was derived from an import.

is_modified.description: Whether the need was modified by needextend.

jinja_content.description: Whether the content was pre-processed by jinja.

layout.description: Key of the layout, which is used to render the need.

lineno.description: Line number where the need is defined (None if external).

parts.description: Mapping of parts, a.k.a. sub-needs, IDs to data that overrides the need's data

post_template.description: The template key, if the post_content was created from a jinja template.

pre_template.description: The template key, if the pre_content was created from a jinja template.

signature.description: Derived from a docutils desc_name node.

style.description: Comma-separated list of CSS classes (all appended by `needs_style_`).

template.description: The template key, if the content was created from a jinja template.
